topic: Complete signed-monotone counterfactual identification for finite binary semi-Markovian causal diagrams. Given a signed local-monotonicity set M, any finite menu Z of observational/interventional population laws, and any positive-denominator unnested conditional counterfactual query Q, construct a signed order-annotated Ancestral Multi-world Network and canonical order-normal event form; define a terminating M-CTFID procedure that factors order-normal cells over districts and uses ctf-calculus transformations; prove it returns a finite identifying functional iff Q is identified, and otherwise compiles its FAIL trace into two legal finite order-respecting response-type SCMs agreeing on all Z but disagreeing on Q. Replace the ordinary AMWN XOR converse with composable signed isotone threshold gadgets, recover ordinary CTFID when M is empty and all successful M-ID outputs, give the explicit response-type-count termination bound, and add empirical-cell plug-in inference under fixed positive denominators. Use Plecko–Bareinboim's Causal Fairness Analysis toolkit and Maiti's M-ID implementation as consumers.

open_problems.open_problem: Give a sound-and-complete identification calculus for positive-denominator conditional counterfactual queries in finite binary semi-Markovian diagrams with signed local-monotonicity constraints and an arbitrary finite menu of observational and interventional laws.

source_refs.claim: M-ID is sound, but the conclusion explicitly calls a sufficient-and-necessary algorithm for general identification under monotonicity an important open research question.
source_refs.author: Aurghya Maiti, Drago Plecko, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: CUT and Ctf-ID give a complete algorithm for nested counterfactual identification from arbitrary combinations of observational and experimental laws, without signed monotonicity restrictions.
source_refs.author: Juan D. Correa, Sanghack Lee, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: AMWNs are sound and complete for counterfactual independences and ctf-calculus transforms counterfactual quantities, but neither object records signed order restrictions on mechanisms.
source_refs.author: Juan D. Correa, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.excerpt: Give an explicit map from source laws to the district factors requested by the ID recursion.
What remains open is the actual flagship deliverable: a theorem-level separation / strict-extension / equivalence.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The ordinary completeness theory treats response assignments as unrestricted except for graphical compatibility, whereas signed monotonicity restricts every binary response table to be isotone after sign-normalizing its parents. M-ID exploits some local reductions but explicitly does not prove necessity. The prior multi-source run independently exposes the other load-bearing gap: heterogeneous source laws must be typed and mapped to the district kernels consumed by the recursion. A complete result therefore needs one order-aware normal form that composes signed restrictions across worlds, districts, conditional-event denominators, and all menu regimes, rather than replaying ordinary source-cover factorization.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A terminating M-CTFID procedure that returns a finite menu-law functional exactly when Q is invariant over all compatible signed-monotone SCMs, returns a checkable nonidentification certificate otherwise, and reduces extensionally to ordinary CTFID when M is empty.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves from query-specific monotonicity results to a graph-wide algorithm and ends by isolating completeness as the missing endpoint.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Counterfactuals may fail ordinary nonparametric identification -> local signed shape restrictions recover important special cases -> a sound general M-ID procedure exists -> the destination is a necessary-and-sufficient monotonicity-aware calculus.

method_exemplars.technique: Counterfactual unnesting, ctf-factorization over confounded components, and failure-to-countermodel completeness for arbitrary observational and experimental inputs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the same query-and-data-menu problem after removing signed response-table restrictions, so every ordinary normalization, factorization, and converse step has a precise order-aware analogue.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct AMWNs and license counterfactual transformations by the three-rule ctf-calculus.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested canonical object is an AMWN augmented with sign and parent-assignment order annotations.

method_exemplars.technique: Compile graphical identification output into estimators and prove asymptotic linearity, robustness, and efficiency properties.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It models how a complete symbolic ID output can feed explicit estimation and limit theory rather than leave inference external.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a composable finite response-type countermodel compiler for signed-monotone Ctf failures, replacing unrestricted parity gadgets by order-respecting isotone threshold gadgets and giving an explicit support-adaptive certificate-size bound.

source_refs.claim: The CTFIDU+ converse constructs agreeing-input, disagreeing-target SCMs using mod-2 parent sums and a flipped last response bit.
source_refs.author: Arvind Raghavan, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: M-ID supplies sound reductions under signed local monotonicity but explicitly leaves full completeness open.
source_refs.author: Aurghya Maiti, Drago Plecko, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: Every finite discrete counterfactual law has a canonical finite-response SCM representation, but the construction is not a signed-isotone converse compiler.
source_refs.author: Junzhe Zhang, Jin Tian, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.excerpt: Replace the unrestricted response-law simplex with a latent-DAG or district-factorized response-type construction.
The field-tier structural-zero lift requires a genuinely new support-hypergraph/matroid project.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The ordinary converse separates models through parity: the 2026 proof explicitly uses mod-2 sums of latent parents and flips one target bit. Parity is nonmonotone in each input and is illegal when an incident edge has a prescribed sign. The failed prior hedge proposal adds a separate legality warning: perturbing an unrestricted response-law simplex is insufficient unless the result arises from a district-factorized SCM. The first proof step that must change is the local hedge/thicket countermodel encoding; it must preserve every menu law using only composable signed-isotone response tables. Structural-zero cells also change the legal up-set/down-set count, so the witness and its termination bound must be support-adaptive. Focused searches found M-ID and unrestricted converses but no signed-isotone Ctf witness construction; this is a bounded-search inference.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A constructive theorem mapping every relevant FAIL trace to two explicit finite district-factorized signed-isotone SCMs equal on all supplied laws and unequal on Q, with a computable response-type count and termination bound, or a counterexample delimiting the traces for which such compilation is impossible.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames completeness, rather than more isolated formulas, as the open endpoint of monotonicity-aware identification.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Monotonicity licenses new reductions -> M-ID exploits them soundly -> completeness requires proving every remaining failure is genuine -> genuine failure under signed mechanisms needs a legal order-preserving countermodel.

method_exemplars.technique: Compile ctf-hedge and ctf-thicket failures into two SCMs through regime-indexed bit encodings and an AMWN-local parity separation bit.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It produces the exact agreeing-input, disagreeing-target certificate required here; its parity gadget is the first component incompatible with signed isotonicity.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace arbitrary latent mechanisms by finitely many canonical response functions and encode all population-law constraints over their masses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Finite canonical response types are the natural carrier for a legal monotone witness and for the requested certificate-size bound.

open_problems.open_problem: Derive sharp identified intervals for positive-denominator conditional counterfactual queries under signed local monotonicity and arbitrary finite observational/interventional data menus by optimizing over signed-isotone canonical response types.

source_refs.claim: Canonical finite SCMs reduce arbitrary-data counterfactual bounding to polynomial programming and yield optimal bounds, without a general signed-local-monotonicity specialization.
source_refs.author: Junzhe Zhang, Jin Tian, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: AutoBounds computes sharp discrete causal bounds through polynomial programming and can encode substantive restrictions, but gives no monotonicity-specific graphical characterization for arbitrary conditional Ctf inputs.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: M-ID targets point identification under local monotonicity and does not return a sharp identified set when its sufficient reductions fail.
source_refs.author: Aurghya Maiti, Drago Plecko, Elias Bareinboim

open_problems.why_unsolved: General canonical-SCM and AutoBounds formulations range over unrestricted response functions unless additional constraints are encoded, while M-ID uses signed monotonicity only for exact symbolic reductions. The first changed proof step is the canonical-model reduction: each local response support must be restricted to the up-sets or down-sets induced by signed parents, and a conditional query becomes a fractional polynomial objective whose denominator must remain positive. A bounded search found special monotonicity bounds and general-purpose optimizers, but no theorem establishing sharpness, attainment, and singleton-collapse equivalence for this full signed-local, arbitrary-menu conditional setting.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite fractional-polynomial or equivalent linearized optimization characterization whose extrema are attained by compatible signed-isotone SCMs, with a theorem that its interval collapses to a singleton exactly when Q is identified.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates partial identification as the principled continuation after exact Ctf-ID failure and formulates the arbitrary-source bounding problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Many counterfactuals are not point identified -> heterogeneous population laws still constrain compatible SCMs -> canonical finite response types make those constraints computable -> signed monotonicity should further shrink the sharp region for conditional targets.

method_exemplars.technique: Canonical finite-SCM reduction followed by polynomial optimization over response-type masses, with a proof of optimal counterfactual bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired object uses the same program after deleting non-isotone response tables and adding a positive-denominator fractional target.

method_exemplars.technique: Use dual relaxations and spatial branch-and-bound to maintain valid outer ranges and certify epsilon-sharpness for discrete causal polynomial programs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the computational proof strategy for certifying extrema when the signed response-type program remains nonlinear.

method_exemplars.technique: Bootstrap randomly perturbed linear-program value functions and prove uniform validity for set-identified parameters defined by linear moments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After a linear-fractional transformation, signed response-type bound endpoints are value functions of the same structural form.

open_problems.open_problem: Compile every successful finite signed-monotone counterfactual identification formula into a representation-invariant empirical-cell estimator with an explicit limit law and valid confidence interval under fixed positive denominators, including ties between equivalent order-normal derivations.

source_refs.claim: The paper reports bootstrap confidence intervals in examples but proves no general limit theorem for arbitrary M-ID output formulas.
source_refs.author: Aurghya Maiti, Drago Plecko, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: This work compiles a broad class of ordinary hidden-variable graphical effect formulas into estimators with influence-function theory, but not signed multi-source conditional counterfactual formulas.
source_refs.author: Rohit Bhattacharya, Razieh Nabi, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: For discrete data, empirical-measure plug-ins for fixed smooth g-formulas are regular and asymptotically linear; signed multi-regime Ctf formula trees lie outside that scope.
source_refs.author: F. Richard Guo, Emilija Perković, Andrea Rotnitzky

source_refs.excerpt: sqrt(n)(hat Phi_n-Phi(p)) converges in distribution to Phi'_p(Z).
Define a sample derivative map using estimated active faces, bootstrap weights, and a near-tie tuning sequence.

open_problems.why_unsolved: A successful M-CTFID output can contain signed sums, district products, marginalizations, and a quotient combining cells from independently sampled regimes. Existing discrete plug-in theory covers a fixed smooth functional, while the prior proposal covers finite max/min envelopes and was itself left to prove. Distinct calculus traces may also be population-equivalent but differ near empirical zeros or derivation ties. The first changed proof step is therefore to establish a canonical representation on a denominator-bounded domain and differentiate its generated rational expression jointly in every regime-specific multinomial cell vector, using a directional derivative and tie-aware bootstrap only where the canonical map is nonsmooth.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A recursive derivative compiler and theorem giving a representation-invariant asymptotic linear or directional-Gaussian limit, consistently estimated variance or tie-aware bootstrap law, and stated confidence-interval coverage for every successful formula on denominator-at-least-kappa laws.

writing_exemplar.why: Its introduction is organized around the practical gap between complete symbolic identification and usable statistical estimation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Graphical algorithms identify many causal targets -> complicated output functionals deter empirical use -> estimator construction should be compiled from the identification proof -> signed conditional counterfactual formulas need the same bridge with representation-invariant inference.

method_exemplars.technique: Treat a discrete identifying formula as a smooth functional of empirical cell probabilities, calculate its influence function, and prove regular asymptotic linearity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A finite-cell M-CTFID output with its denominator bounded away from zero is likewise a rational functional, now jointly of several regime laws.

method_exemplars.technique: Recursively translate graphical identification factorizations into estimating functions and prove robustness and efficiency properties.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest identification-to-estimation compiler, though the new grammar includes signed reductions and conditional quotients.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate the directional derivative of a nonsmooth finite-dimensional map and use a derivative-aware bootstrap at active-set ties.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Equivalent order-normal branches can create the same finite-dimensional kinks as tied active faces.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the inclusion-minimal signed edge-monotonicity sets and observational/interventional data menus identifying each variable-specific direct, indirect, spurious, and post-treatment-conditioned contrast in the finite binary Standard Fairness Model.

source_refs.claim: Causal Fairness Analysis organizes direct, indirect, spurious, and variable-specific contrasts and asks which causal assumptions make these quantities computable.
source_refs.author: Drago Plecko, Elias Bareinboim
source_refs.venue: Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning

source_refs.claim: For the Standard Fairness Graph, local monotonicity identifies selected post-treatment-conditioned effects that are not identified without it, rather than a complete minimal-assumption frontier for the fairness map.
source_refs.author: Aurghya Maiti, Drago Plecko, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: CUT and Ctf-ID handle nested direct, indirect, and spurious counterfactuals from arbitrary surrogate experiments but do not exploit signed local monotonicity.
source_refs.author: Juan D. Correa, Sanghack Lee, Elias Bareinboim

open_problems.why_unsolved: The fairness monograph supplies the destination family and ordinary causal-assumption recipes, while Maiti et al. establish monotonicity-based identification only for selected post-treatment effects. The first changed proof step is to unnest every fairness-map query while retaining its factual conditioning event, then solve the order-constrained identification problem across every candidate signed-edge set and source menu. Focused searches found the selected formulas and general fairness decompositions, but no complete inclusion-minimal frontier; this absence claim is limited to the conducted search.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite lookup characterization assigning every named fairness-map contrast all inclusion-minimal signed-monotonicity and data-menu conditions with an identifying functional, plus two compatible fairness SCMs proving nonidentification when no listed condition holds.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation connects observed disparities to mechanism-specific explanations and organizes the destination queries in a Fairness Map and Cookbook.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Observed parity metrics cannot explain mechanisms -> direct, indirect, and spurious contrasts provide the decomposition -> practical use requires identification from available data and assumptions -> signed monotonicity may provide the missing minimal-assumption frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply counterfactual unnesting and complete Ctf-ID factorization to direct, indirect, and spurious nested contrasts under arbitrary surrogate experiments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It resolves the unrestricted nested-query preprocessing and data-fusion component of the requested fairness classification.

method_exemplars.technique: Use monotonicity reduction and difference rules to turn cross-world post-treatment cells into identifiable interventional factors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The paper proves selected members of the requested frontier and supplies the mechanism that must be systematized.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct efficient influence functions and multiply robust estimators for direct and indirect counterfactual functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Identified direct and indirect fairness components inherit the same multi-factor mediation structure.

open_problems.open_problem: For a finite binary counterfactual query and signed local-monotonicity set M, characterize in observable cells when M point-identifies the query, strictly tightens its identified set, or is redundant relative to unrestricted response types.

source_refs.excerpt: Mediator monotonicity can tighten only the upper PN endpoint.
Replace the generic support-slack equivalence with an explicit irredundant observable cell/facet characterization.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Exact response-type enumeration refuted the prior two-endpoint claim: one endpoint is invariant to mediator monotonicity while only the other can tighten. Deleting order-violating response types therefore does not reveal whether M is informative for a query. The missing step is to relate the signed-order face of each response polytope to the query-optimal unrestricted faces through irredundant observable cell or facet conditions, rather than the circular test that two already-computed endpoint values differ.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient finite facial characterization in observable cells that partitions compatible laws into point-identification, strict set-tightening, and monotonicity-redundant regimes for Q under M.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates how mediator information can sharpen causal-attribution bounds and asks when the extra structure is informative.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Weak assumptions give broad attribution bounds -> mediator structure may add information -> signed restrictions delete response types -> determine exactly which observable laws turn that deletion into identification or strict gain.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent binary SCMs by response types, impose observed-cell constraints, and prove sharp endpoints through finite primal-dual linear programming.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested partition compares unrestricted and signed-order faces of the same finite response-type fiber.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive directional derivatives of finite max/min envelopes and bootstrap them through estimated active faces.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Observable activation conditions create nonsmooth transitions precisely where signed monotonicity begins to tighten a bound.

literature_map:
1. Maiti, Plecko, and Bareinboim (AAAI 2025) is the decisive gap anchor: M-ID is sound and subsumes earlier monotonicity results, but its conclusion explicitly labels a complete necessary-and-sufficient monotonicity algorithm open.
2. The same paper encodes positive and negative local edge monotonicity, proves monotonicity reduction and difference rules, and identifies selected LATE, LNDE/LNIE, probability-of-causation, and post-treatment fairness queries.
3. Shpitser and Pearl (JMLR 2008) established complete ordinary counterfactual identification from lower causal-hierarchy layers, supplying the foundational unrestricted completeness template.
4. Correa, Lee, and Bareinboim (NeurIPS 2021; arXiv:2107.03190) give CUT and complete Ctf-ID for nested counterfactuals from arbitrary observational and experimental laws.
5. Lee, Correa, and Bareinboim (UAI 2020) give complete gID for arbitrary surrogate-experiment menus through hedgelets and thickets at the interventional level.
6. Correa and Bareinboim (ICML 2025) introduce AMWNs and ctf-calculus, making counterfactual independences and transformations explicit but without signed order constraints.
7. Raghavan and Bareinboim (arXiv:2602.23541, 2026) extend completeness to realizable Layer-3 inputs; their converse explicitly uses mod-2 latent-bit gadgets, exposing the proof boundary under monotonicity.
8. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (ICML 2022; arXiv:2110.05690) prove a canonical finite-SCM reduction and optimal polynomial-program bounds from arbitrary observational and experimental laws.
9. Duarte et al. (JASA 2024; arXiv:2109.13471) automate sharp discrete causal bounds with polynomial optimization, dual relaxations, branch-and-bound, and epsilon-sharpness guarantees.
10. Balke and Pearl's response-function linear-program tradition and Tian–Pearl probability-of-causation results are older anchors showing how monotonicity deletes response types and can collapse bounds.
11. Plecko and Bareinboim (FnTML 2024; arXiv:2207.11385) supply the Causal Fairness Analysis consumer family: direct, indirect, spurious, and variable-specific counterfactual contrasts.
12. Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser (JMLR 2022; arXiv:2003.12659), Guo–Perković–Rotnitzky (Biometrika 2023), and Tchetgen Tchetgen–Shpitser (AoS 2012) supply adjacent identification-to-inference and influence-function machinery.
13. Cho and Russell (JBES 2024; arXiv:1810.03180) and Fang–Santos (ReStud 2019) provide inference for optimization-value and directionally differentiable maps relevant to bounds and branch ties.
14. Bounded searches found general partial-ID optimizers and special monotonicity results, but no complete signed-monotone Ctf calculus, no order-respecting replacement for parity converse gadgets, and no general inference compiler for arbitrary M-ID outputs.
prior_proposal_map:
The current qid scm_monotone_ctf_complete_calculus has only run-state/log metadata and no earlier proposal core or reviewer JSON.
The closest converse substrate is failed scm_cs_hedge_completeness/v1; all three proto-core angles, its README, and seven angle reviews were inspected. Its reviewers expose district-factorization, binary-witness, and termination obligations, while the bank record warns that a terminal failure need not itself imply nonidentification.
Downgraded eid_data_fusion_k_source/v1 supplies the arbitrary-menu analogue; its proposal and angle reviewers repeatedly request an explicit source-law-to-district-factor map and a genuine equivalence frontier against SS-ID, gID, and do-search.
Downgraded scm_mediator_monotonicity_pn_v1/mediator_defier_gap supplies the signed-order response-face warning: exact enumeration refuted simultaneous endpoint tightening, leaving only upper-endpoint gain and motivating an observable activation/redundancy frontier.
Downgraded scm_fortified_proxy_threshold/v1 supplies a constrained-function-space count plus the unresolved structural-zero/support-pattern lift and explicit termination obligations.
Failed scm_prox_recant_pid/v1 was inspected for the nested recanting-witness boundary, but that extension was not retained because this topic fixes unnested conditionals.
The counterfactual-fairness bank entry was inspected as a consumer-adjacent record but had no proposal/reviewer artifact usable as a load-bearing source.
No prior artifact in doc/research names CTFID, AMWN, M-ID, Maiti's implementation, or a signed-isotone threshold replacement directly; these are cross-catalogue synthesis points rather than duplicates.
